shadow:
There is a kind of guarding so quiet it does not feel like guarding at all. It feels like taste. Like good judgment. You let people partway in, you keep a little of yourself held back, and you call this being careful, which it is, partly.

Vanity is the love of your own separateness. Not the loud sort that wants a mirror. The fine sort, the sort that says I see things more clearly than the people around me, and never says it out loud. Underneath the calm the feelings are running hot, and the whole arrangement exists to keep them from spilling, because somewhere early on a fear took hold that love coming in too fast would be more than a person could hold.

Most people read this distance as a personality, the way they simply are. That is the misread. The held-back warmth is not absent. It is dammed. And a dam is not the end of a river. There is an ocean behind it, waiting, and the wall was only ever built by a frightened child who thought it was protecting something. The wall can be questioned. That is the opening, and it starts the moment you stop calling the distance taste.
repressive: Some people meet the fear by going untouchable. They decide they are simply clearer than the people around them, agree on the surface, withdraw underneath, and let no one close enough to test it. It reads as composure. It is a locked door.
reactive: Others turn the sharp eye outward as a weapon. They have a real gift for words and they use it to find the soft place in someone and press. The hurt they deal is rarely planned. It is just quick, and it tends to cost them the people they wanted.
gift:
The turn happens when the sharp eye swings around. The same instinct that read everyone else, that knew within seconds who was faking and who was not, gets pointed back at the one who owns it. That is uncomfortable in a way the old habit never was. It is also where the gift lives.

Discrimination is honest attention. It is the willingness to look at your own holding back and call it what it is, fear, rather than dress it as discernment. Once you can see the wall as a wall, you can start letting the world past it. The emotions you braced against turn out to rise and then settle. They do not drown anyone. You begin to remember what love felt like before you learned to ration it.

This gift has a sound to it. When a person speaks from the warmed place instead of the guarded one, the voice carries differently, and other people feel it before they can say why. It reaches toward something it has not named yet, something pure, and it will not pretend a counterfeit is the real thing. The closer it gets to that, the less it wants to be alone.
siddhi:
Far enough in, the wall is simply not there, and you notice it the way you notice a noise stopping. The careful management of who gets close, the rationing, the held breath, all of it has nothing left to do.

Purity is what vanity was reaching for the whole time, badly. Vanity loved a self it thought was separate. Here the heart remembers it was never separate, that there is one thing wearing every face, and so there is nothing left to defend and no one left outside to defend against. Lock such a person away, take everything from them, and the love still runs. Nothing external can reach it, because from here there is no external. It is all one heart, and a life lived from that knows it.

The people who carry this rarely stand out. They live small, plain lives, often unnoticed. And looking back down the road from here, the old guardedness was not a flaw to be ashamed of. It was the dam, and the dam was holding the ocean. The ocean was always the point.
